facts.fact: The page states that QR codes have been around since 1994.
facts.quote: QR codes have been around since 1994, but their use in TV advertising really took off after two converging trends:

facts.fact: The page attributes to Statista a claim that QR code scans in the U.S. increased by over 400% between 2020 and 2024.
facts.quote: According to Statista, QR code scans in the U.S. increased by over 400% between 2020 and 2024.

facts.fact: The page states that the 2022 Coinbase Super Bowl ad, which featured only a bouncing QR code, generated over 20 million scans in 60 seconds.
facts.quote: The 2022 Coinbase Super Bowl ad that featured nothing but a bouncing QR code generated over 20 million scans in 60 seconds.

facts.fact: The page recommends that a QR code in a TV ad occupy at least 15 to 20% of the screen area.
facts.quote: The QR code should occupy at least 15 to 20% of the screen area.

facts.fact: The page cites a typical TV viewing distance of 6 to 10 feet.
facts.quote: A tiny code in the corner won't scan reliably from 6 to 10 feet away (typical viewing distance).

facts.fact: The page recommends placing the QR code in the last 5 to 10 seconds of a commercial.
facts.quote: Place the code on screen during the portion of the ad where you want viewers to take action (typically the last 5 to 10 seconds).

facts.fact: The page recommends keeping the QR code visible for at least 5 seconds, ideally the final 7 to 10 seconds of a 30-second spot.
facts.quote: Give viewers at least 5 seconds with the QR code visible. Ideally, show it for the final 7 to 10 seconds of a 30-second spot.

facts.fact: The page sets a landing page target of page load time under 3 seconds for QR code traffic.
facts.quote: Page load time under 3 seconds is the target.

facts.fact: The page says short-form ads of 15 seconds or less are a weak use case for QR codes because there is not enough time for viewers to scan.
facts.quote: Short-form ads (15 seconds or less). Fifteen seconds isn't enough time to tell a story and give viewers time to scan.

facts.fact: The page says audiences 65 and older scan QR codes at significantly lower rates, and recommends phone numbers or URLs for that audience.
facts.quote: Audiences 65+. While QR code adoption has increased across all ages, older demographics scan at significantly lower rates.

facts.fact: The page recommends using a dynamic QR code so the destination URL can be changed after the ad is running.
facts.quote: Use dynamic QR codes. Static QR codes permanently link to one URL. Dynamic codes let you change the destination URL after the ad is already running.

facts.fact: The page states that QR code scan rates on TV ads typically range from 0.5% to 2% of total ad impressions.
facts.quote: QR code scan rates on TV ads typically range from 0.5% to 2% of total ad impressions.

facts.fact: The page gives an illustrative example in which a CTV campaign with 100,000 impressions and a 1% scan rate generates 1,000 website visits.
facts.quote: A [CTV campaign](https://adwave.com/resources/what-is-connected-tv-advertising) delivering 100,000 impressions with a 1% scan rate generates 1,000 website visits

facts.fact: The page states that CTV viewers typically sit 5 to 8 feet from the screen in a living room couch setup.
facts.quote: CTV viewers typically sit 5 to 8 feet from the screen (living room couch).

facts.fact: Citing Statista, the page says adults 18 to 44 account for over 70% of QR code scans.
facts.quote: According to Statista, adults 18 to 44 account for over 70% of QR code scans.

facts.fact: The page states that CTV ads are typically non-skippable with 90%+ completion rates.
facts.quote: CTV ads are typically non-skippable with 90%+ completion rates.

facts.fact: The page recommends working the QR code into the final 7 to 10 seconds of a 30-second TV spot.
facts.quote: Work the QR code into the final 7 to 10 seconds of your 30-second spot.

facts.fact: The page recommends that a QR code landing page load in under 3 seconds.
facts.quote: Load in under 3 seconds

facts.fact: The page advises resizing the QR code if it does not scan reliably at 8 feet on a 50-inch screen.
facts.quote: If it doesn't scan reliably at 8 feet on a 50-inch screen, resize it.

facts.fact: The page recommends testing QR codes at typical viewing distances of 6 to 10 feet on actual TVs before running a campaign.
facts.quote: Test at typical viewing distances (6 to 10 feet) on actual TVs before running the campaign.

facts.fact: The page states that scanning a QR code takes 2 to 3 seconds, while typing a URL from memory takes 30 seconds or more.
facts.value: 2 to 3 seconds vs 30 or more seconds
facts.quote: Scanning a QR code takes 2 to 3 seconds. Typing a URL from memory takes 30 seconds or more

facts.fact: In an illustrative HVAC example, the page's suggested TV ad prompt is 'Scan to book your $49 spring tune-up.'
facts.quote: The prompt: "Scan to book your $49 spring tune-up."

facts.fact: The page states, without citing a source, that restaurants using QR codes in TV ads often see 2 to 3 times more online reservations during campaign periods than ads without a scan option.
facts.quote: Restaurants that use QR codes in TV ads often see 2 to 3 times more online reservations during campaign periods

facts.fact: In an illustrative retail example, the page's suggested TV prompt offers 15% off for scanning.
facts.quote: The prompt: "Scan for 15% off, online or in-store."

facts.fact: The page's example conversion assumption is that 10% of visitors from a QR scan convert, which would produce 100 leads or customers from 1,000 visits.
facts.quote: If 10% of those visitors convert, that's 100 new leads or customers
